blocks.text: 108 מוּסָף לְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה 108
uncertainties: The running header is small, so its pointing (מוּסָף and the others) is only partly legible.

blocks.text: יוֹם הַדִּין. לִפְקוֹד עַל צְבָא מָרוֹם בַּדִּין. כִּי לֹא יִזְכּוּ בְעֵינֶיךָ בַּדִּין. וְכָל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם תַּעֲבִיר (כ״א יַעֲבְרוּן) לְפָנֶיךָ כִּבְנֵי מָרוֹן.
uncertainties: The page begins mid-sentence: יוֹם הַדִּין continues the previous page.
(כ״א יַעֲבְרוּן) is small type in parentheses. It is a variant reading ('another version: יַעֲבְרוּן') for תַּעֲבִיר. It is not a Shabbat addition.
The opening word of the first line, יום, looks like it has a holam, but the ink is light.
Unsure whether בְעֵינֶיךָ and כִּבְנֵי have a dagesh in the first letter. The scan is ambiguous.
Small rubric word set inline before כְּבַקָּרַת. It means 'cantor', who starts here.

blocks.text: כְּבַקָּרַת רוֹעֶה עֶדְרוֹ. מַעֲבִיר צֹאנוֹ תַּחַת שִׁבְטוֹ. כֵּן תַּעֲבִיר וְתִסְפּוֹר וְתִמְנֶה. וְתִפְקוֹד נֶפֶשׁ כָּל חָי. וְתַחְתּוֹךְ קִצְבָה לְכָל בְּרִיָּה. וְתִכְתּוֹב אֶת גְּזַר דִּינָם:
uncertainties: The vowel under the ayin of עֶדְרוֹ looks like segol, but it could be hataf.
The vowel under the shin of שִׁבְטוֹ is hard to read.

blocks.text: בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יִכָּתֵבוּן. וּבְיוֹם (צוֹם) כִּפּוּר יֵחָתֵמוּן. כַּמָּה יַעַבְרוּן. וְכַמָּה יִבָּרֵאוּן. מִי יִחְיֶה. וּמִי יָמוּת. מִי בְקִצּוֹ. וּמִי לֹא בְקִצּוֹ. מִי בָאֵשׁ. וּמִי בַמַּיִם. מִי בַחֶרֶב. (וּמִי בַחַיָּה.) וּמִי בָרָעָב. (וּמִי בַצָּמָא.) מִי בָרַעַשׁ. וּמִי בַמַּגֵּפָה. (מִי בַחֲנִיקָה וּמִי בִסְקִילָה.) מִי יָנוּחַ. וּמִי יָנוּעַ. מִי יִשָּׁקֵט. וּמִי יִטָּרֵף. מִי יִשָּׁלֵו. וּמִי יִתְיַסָּר. מִי יָרוּם (כ״א יוּרָם.) וּמִי יִשָּׁפֵל. מִי יֵעָשֵׁר. וּמִי יֵעָנִי:
uncertainties: (צוֹם) is printed in full-size type inside parentheses. It reads as a word to insert ('day of the fast of atonement'). The page gives no condition for it, and it is not marked as a Shabbat addition.
These are printed small inside parentheses: (וּמִי בַחַיָּה.), (וּמִי בַצָּמָא.) and (מִי בַחֲנִיקָה וּמִי בִסְקִילָה.). The page does not say when or by whom they are said.
(כ״א יוּרָם.) is a variant reading for יָרוּם.
In כַּמָּה יַעַבְרוּן the two words are tightly spaced and could be joined by a maqaf. יַעַבְרוּן seems to carry patach plus a small mark that may be a meteg or a hataf. Unclear.

Three small unpointed words, each set directly above one of the large words below: צום over וּתְשׁוּבָה, קול over וּתְפִלָּה, ממון over וּצְדָקָה. They are glosses on those words, not sound names. Layout is one row with three entries; read right to left it goes צום, קול, ממון.

blocks.text: וּתְשׁוּבָה וּתְפִלָּה וּצְדָקָה מַעֲבִירִין אֶת רֹעַ הַגְּזֵרָה:
uncertainties: The first line, וּתְשׁוּבָה וּתְפִלָּה וּצְדָקָה, is printed in very large display type. The second line is in medium type.
רֹעַ could be the plene spelling רוֹעַ. The letter after resh is not clear.

blocks.text: קה״ל בעטעט ביז ושמנו קראת בשמך.
uncertainties: This is a German instruction in Hebrew script: 'the congregation prays until ושמנו קראת בשמך'.
The first word is printed as a ligature or abbreviation of קהל. Unsure whether it is קה״ל or קהל.

blocks.text: כִּי כְשִׁמְךָ כֵּן תְּהִלָּתֶךָ. קָשֶׁה לִכְעוֹס וְנוֹחַ לִרְצוֹת. כִּי לֹא תַחְפּוֹץ בְּמוֹת הַמֵּת. כִּי אִם בְּשׁוּבוֹ מִדַּרְכּוֹ וְחָיָה. וְעַד יוֹם מוֹתוֹ תְּחַכֶּה לוֹ. אִם יָשׁוּב מִיַּד תְּקַבְּלוֹ:
uncertainties: The kaf of כְשִׁמְךָ may have a dagesh.
לֹא and תַחְפּוֹץ are printed with almost no space between them (לֹאתַחְפּוֹץ).
A tiny abbreviation before אֱמֶת. It looks most like ח׳ (חזן, cantor), but it could be ק׳ (קהל, congregation).

blocks.text: אֱמֶת, כִּי אַתָּה הוּא יוֹצְרָם. וְיוֹדֵעַ יִצְרָם. כִּי הֵם בָּשָׂר וָדָם: אָדָם
uncertainties: The page ends mid-sentence at אָדָם, which continues on the next page.
There is a comma after אֱמֶת.

blocks.text: is to be considered in judgment’ for they have no merit in Thine eyes in judgment. Then Thou dost cause all who come into the world to pass before Thee like lambs. Just as a shepherd controlling his herd makes his flock pass beneath his staff, so dost Thou cause to pass, count, reckon and consider every living soul and Thou dost appoint a limit for every creature and inscribe their verdict.
uncertainties: The page begins mid-sentence and closes a quotation that opened on the previous page. The closing mark is a right single quote ’.

blocks.text: On the New Year they are inscribed and on the Day of Atonement they are sealed, how many shall pass away and how many shall be born, who shall live and who shall die, who at his proper time and who before his time, who by fire and who by water, who by the sword and who by hunger, who by the storm and who by the plague, who shall have rest and who unrest, who shall find repose and who shall be harassed, who shall be calm and who chastised, who raised high and who laid low, who enriched and who impoverished.
uncertainties: There is a stray dot in the left margin beside 'and how many shall be born'. It is probably a print speck.
The English does not translate the parenthetical Hebrew additions: wild beast, thirst, strangling, stoning.

blocks.text: Yet Penitence, Prayer and Charity avert the disaster of the decree.
uncertainties: Printed as two centered lines, the first one in larger or bolder type.

blocks.text: For as Thy Name so is Thy fame. Hard to anger and light to appease, Thou dost not desire the death of the man condemned to death, but that he should turn back from his way and live; until the day of his death dost Thou wait for him, should he repent, Thou wilt at once receive him. In truth Thou art their Creator and Thou knowest their impulse for they are flesh and blood. Man is formed from dust and
uncertainties: The page ends mid-sentence.

notes: Both scans are printed page 108. s236 is the Hebrew side and s237 is the facing English side.
Neither page has biblical citation blocks, footnotes or bottom text.
No cantillation accents could be seen on s236. The few small marks near vowels may be meteg, but this is uncertain.
The English page has no rubrics. The German קה״ל instruction and the חזן and ח׳ speaker markers are not rendered in English.
Overlapping parts of the enlarged bands were checked against the full-page images, and each block appears only once.
